Just then, the crowd was shushed to hear the chosson give the customary pilpul. As was to be expected, Binyamin spoke wonderfully, displaying vast Torah knowledge. Reb Moshe,

Reb Baruch, and Reb Aharon all joined the ensuing Torah discussion, elaborating, debating, and exploring various ideas mentioned in Binyamin’s speech. There was one person who,

throughout it all, didn’t say a word. The Baal Shem’s messenger, Reb Yehuda Zusha.

The whole time, Reb Yehuda Zusha sat quietly, staring absently to the side. Every now and again he’d take a bite of food. It seemed that he hadn’t a clue of what was going on.

When it was time for bentching, Reb Aharon stood up to speak. His eyes glistened as he spoke, holding a silver becher full of wine. “Honored guests! It is a real z’chus for me to be here, to have

my daughter—me, simple, poor, Aharonchik—engaged to the son

of Harav Hagaon Reb Baruch! It was only because our holy Rebbi and guide, Rabbi Yoel Baal Shem of Zamostch, directed us to join our children in marriage. Now, the heiliker Baal Shem has sent a messenger to join us today. And as chazal say, ‘Shlucho shel adam k’moso1—A messenger is considered like the person who sent him.’ Therefore, with the permission of my mechutan, Reb Baruch, I’d like to give the

cup of wine to the Baal Shem’s representative and honor him with leading the bentching.”

Everyone’s eyes now turned to Reb Yehuda Zusha, who was shifting uncomfortably in his seat. After a few moments, he cleared

his throat loudly. “I-I’m not used to leading the bentching,” he said.

Reb Baruch placed a hand on Reb Yehuda Zusha’s shoulder. “The

to only davening and bentching from a siddur.” A siddur was brought, and Reb Yehuda Zusha squinted to see the letters on

Reb Moshe kept his eyes firmly planted on the floor for the rest of bentching. After it was over, he walked over to Reb Baruch’s seat. He leaned over, whispering so no one would hear: “I’m sorry Reb Baruch. You must be so ashamed.”

Reb Baruch tilted his head and raised an eyebrow. Clearly, he had no idea what Reb Moshe was talking about.

Reb Moshe explained. “I’m sorry that your Rebbi’s messenger brought shame to this simcha.”

Reb Baruch chuckled. “Oy, mechutan, you shouldn’t have worried. If my Rebbi has sent him here to us, I’m sure it was most fitting for him to be here. I don’t feel that he has in any way embarrassed me, chas v’shalom, nor ruined my simcha.”

my Rebbi would tell me to marry my son to the daughter of a total am ha’aretz2, I wouldn’t hesitate for a moment! How much more so am I happy to marry my son to the daughter of a fine man like Reb Aharon. We are truly fortunate; the kallah is a lovely girl, and her father is a real tzaddik. Reb Aharon is a man who is moser nefesh to educate Jewish children.”

Rabbi Moshe just stared at Reb Baruch for a long moment, dumbfounded. How could a brilliant talmid chacham like Reb Baruch think this way?

A few months later, it was time for the wedding. As soon as Reb Moshe entered the hall, he looked around the room; would Reb Yehuda Zusha be here again? It seemed, after a scan of the crowd, that he wasn’t. Instead, at the head table, seated right next to the chosson, was a man—surely a rav or a dayan, Reb Moshe thought—in a fine silk overcoat, and a glossy brown fur hat.

Reb Baruch had the good sense to arrange for a different messenger, Reb Moshe thought, with relief. As Reb Moshe got closer to the table, though, he realized that while the clothes were new, the face was familiar. It really was Reb Yehuda Zusha again, but in different clothing.

of the discussions at the head table. In fact, he didn’t say much of anything. He just stared ahead, glassy-eyed, as Reb Moshe, Reb Baruch, and the others discussed Torah.

Binyamin gave a brilliant drasha, of course; first explaining a complex Gemara, then raising a number of questions on it, and answering them all with one novel solution. When Binyamin sat down, it was the cue for the talmidei chachamim in the audience to respond and

comment on the ideas he spoke about. It was exactly then that Reb Yehuda Zusha lifted his hand and asked for permission to speak.
